description:
A reading list, read aloud and served as audio: four units, each of which runs and can be tested on its own.

**Reader** is the RSS board — feeds in, a reading list out, and that list published as a feed of its own. **Voice** is a text-to-speech endpoint and nothing else. **Radio** reads a feed, skips what it has already spoken, calls the voice, keeps the audio, and publishes what it has read. **Library** serves the audio, read-only, at an address a player can be pointed at.

What holds them together is deliberately thin, and it is not a wire. The radio reads the reader's output **as a feed**, which is why it does not know the reading list is a SQL table — or that there is a reading list at all; give it any feed and it does the same thing. It reaches the voice and the library by *mount reference*: a board names a service, and the coordinator resolves the address when the board loads. It shares the library's bytes by **naming the same volume**, the way two boards share a database.

Each unit's runtimes keep the unit's own board name, so a unit composed here is the same to a server as a unit opened alone — the same endpoints, the same tables. What the composition qualifies is the runtime id, which is why the voice is addressed as `voice.speech` here and as `speech` when it runs by itself.

Needs hkp-node on port 8080 and hkp-python on port 9000.
